name: Acute Motor and Sensory Axonal Neuropathy
aliases: Acute Motor and Sensory Axonal Guillain-Barré Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Brighton Criteria for Guillain-Barré Syndrome (adapted for AMSAN)

criteria.description: Acute onset of progressive symmetrical weakness affecting both motor and sensory nerves
Electrophysiological studies showing axonal degeneration of motor and sensory nerves
Cerebrospinal fluid showing elevated protein with normal cell count
Exclusion of other causes of acute neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of acute progressive symmetrical motor and sensory weakness with electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy and exclusion of alternative diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: CSF findings may be normal early in disease; electrophysiology is critical for diagnosis.

searchTerms: symmetric weakness in hands and feet
weakness affecting both distal limbs equally
reduced or missing muscle stretch reflexes
numbness and tingling in hands and feet
loss of sensation in fingers and toes
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

common.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction (e.g., tachycardia, blood pressure instability)
searchTerms: problems with heart rate and blood pressure
unstable blood pressure and fast heartbeat

occasional.symptomName: Cranial nerve involvement other than facial nerve
searchTerms: weakness or numbness in face areas

rare.symptomName: Severe autonomic instability leading to arrhythmias

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein with normal white cell count (cytoalbuminologic dissociation)
Elevated inflammatory markers may be present
imaging: MRI of spine may show nerve root enhancement
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; considered an acquired autoimmune neuropathy
other: Electrophysiological studies showing reduced or absent compound muscle action potentials and sensory nerve action potentials consistent with axonal degeneration

distinguishingFeatures: Slower conduction velocities rather than axonal loss

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness leading to respiratory failure
Bulbar muscle weakness causing dysphagia or airway compromise
references: Willison HJ, Jacobs BC, van Doorn PA. Guillain-Barré syndrome. Lancet. 2016 Aug 13;388(10045):717-727.
Orphanet: Acute motor and sensory axonal neuropathy - ORPHA:98917
